findings.reason: §14 must add `reckon/crew/review.py` to its write paths and state how a code review is filed in the committed tree (a code-review destination beside `run/` and `plan/`), which its "No new store, key or option is added" and its two-path write scope both currently forbid; without it the dispatched node is fenced out of the module it must change, or lands a promotion that refuses.
findings.text: §14's deliverable says "The stored code review record is among the review payloads the promotion commits", but the payload returned by `_staging_review_record_by_run` is filed by `review.store_committed_review` (`reckon/crew/review.py:2589`), which requires `names_a_review_subject` — a non-empty `reviewed_run_id` or a `plan_slug` with an integer `plan_version` (`review.py:1756`). A path-only code review carries neither: the nova delivery `code-98773e8b1367.json` has neither field, `names_a_review_subject` returns False, and `store_committed_review` raises `review record names neither a reviewed run nor a plan, so it has no subject to be filed under` (reproduced). nova's committed tree `docs/state/nova/reviews/` holds `plan/` and `run/` and no `code-*` file, so a code review has never been committed. Worse, this call site is `reckon/crew/promotion.py:1261-1279`, which catches the `ValueError` and raises a landing refusal ("cannot store the review record for run … so the landing was rolled back") — so adding the payload as described turns promotion of a code review into a rolled-back landing, not an uncommitted record

findings.reason: §14's mechanism resolves the delivery by the neighbourhood key (`code_review_identity` → `a8eb488cc578`) and never uses the composed id, so the truncated spelling misleads a reader but changes no node's work.
findings.text: §14's "composed as `r-20261015T053316274650`" names a run id that resolves to no run directory and is not the id the delivery records; the code review's `code-review.json` sidecar carries `review_run_id: r-20261015T053316274650-review-code-a8eb488cc578`

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §14's "composed as `r-20261015T053316274650`" names no run or directory; the delivery's own sidecar records the composed id as `r-20261015T053316274650-review-code-a8eb488cc578`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §14 enumerates six cases with a declared negative control (remove the code-review branch; case 1 must fail), so its gate can fail on the unfixed code.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §14's logs land under the crew run directory, a durable path, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §14's new test file and prose are named by mechanism; no plan label, stage name or ticket number reaches a symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §14's mechanism cannot produce its own done-when: `store_committed_review` refuses a review record that names neither a reviewed run nor a plan, which is exactly the `--path` code review §14 is about.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §14 carries one deliverable: promotion stores and commits a code review under the neighbourhood key.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the new section declaration (`s14: implementable`) and the followup `f-tcirbn-s14` point at the section that exists, and no depends-on/informs/gates edge names a node that does not.
